description: Reference for using DAG nodes as LLM-callable tools inside an llm_call's tool_configurations. Complements node_configurations.json (which documents nodes as DAG nodes) by focusing exclusively on the tool-calling perspective: how to declare each node type as a tool, what fields are fixed vs LLM-visible, and complete ready-to-use examples.

tool_configurations.summary: A map on any llm_call node that registers DAG nodes as LLM-callable tools. Keys can be semantic names ('search_flights') or UUIDs (generated by frontends) — both work because the engine uses the 'name' field inside each entry as the effective tool name shown to the LLM.

name.description: Tool name shown to the LLM. Use descriptive function-style names (e.g. 'search_flights'). The engine uses this field — the map key is only a fallback when 'name' is empty.

description.description: What the tool does and when to use it. No need to add general 'always call this tool' rules — the engine auto-injects a tool-use instruction block into the system prompt.

node_type.description: DAG node type to execute when the LLM calls this tool. Must be a registered node type.

node_schema.description: RECOMMENDED parameter strategy. A flat map of field names to NodeSchemaField objects. Fields with 'fixed' are hidden from the LLM. Fields without 'fixed' are exposed to the LLM with their type, description, and constraints. Container fields (type='object') support nested 'properties' for mixed fixed/dynamic sub-fields.

NodeSchemaField.fixed: any — if present, field is hidden from LLM and always set to this value. Supports '${context.key}' and '${ENV_VAR}' resolution.
NodeSchemaField.type: string — JSON Schema type: 'string', 'number', 'boolean', 'object', 'array'. Required for LLM-visible fields.
NodeSchemaField.required: boolean — whether the LLM must supply this field. Only meaningful when 'fixed' is absent.
NodeSchemaField.description: string — description sent to the LLM. Include format expectations and examples.
NodeSchemaField.pattern: string — regex constraint for the LLM (e.g. '^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$' for dates).
NodeSchemaField.properties: object — nested NodeSchemaField map for type='object' containers. Each child can be fixed or LLM-visible.

fixed_config.description: Static values merged into the node inputs before execution. Supports '${context.key}' and '${ENV_VAR}' syntax. Use with node_schema for fixed non-LLM fields, or alone with '$DYNAMIC' placeholders for simple cases.

dynamic_placeholder.description: Set a string value to the literal '$DYNAMIC' to auto-expose it as a required string parameter to the LLM. Limitation: only works ONE level deep inside a container — body.title works, body.metadata.author.name does NOT. For nested or non-string fields, use node_schema instead.

node_config.description: For toolkit nodes only (e.g. tavily_client). The static configuration passed to the underlying toolkit node at construction time (e.g. api_key, max_calls_per_run). Not exposed to the LLM.

expose_sub_tools.description: For toolkit nodes only. Controls which sub-tools are exposed to the LLM. 'all' exposes every sub-tool the toolkit declares. Specific sub-tool names can be listed as an array to expose a subset. When set, the LLM sees '<alias>__<subtool>' as the tool name (e.g. 'web__search', 'web__fetch').

context.description: Dynamic values injected into node_schema or fixed_config via '${context.key}' syntax. Used to pass runtime values (e.g. auth tokens from upstream nodes) into the tool without hardcoding them.

secure.description: When true, the tool output is hashed before being returned to the LLM — real values (e.g. access tokens) are replaced with safe placeholders like '<value_1>'. The engine resolves placeholders back to real values when used in subsequent tool calls via inject_secrets(). Requires DATABASE_URL and SECURE_VALUES_KEY env vars.

enabled_tools.summary: Optional allow-list that unions with the auto-enabled set. Tools defined in tool_configurations are auto-enabled — you do NOT need to list them here. Use enabled_tools only to: (1) enable built-in toolkit tools (Tavily, etc.) not in tool_configurations, or (2) use '*' to expose every available tool including built-ins.
enabled_tools.auto_enabled_behavior: Every key in tool_configurations is automatically enabled. enabled_tools is additive, not a gate. If all your tools are in tool_configurations and none are built-in toolkits, you can omit enabled_tools entirely.
when_to_use: You have built-in toolkit tools (tavily_client, etc.) alongside tool_configurations entries
You want '*' to expose all available tools including built-ins
You want to dynamically enable/disable tools via an upstream node input
when_to_omit: All your tools are defined in tool_configurations and none are built-in toolkits

use_dynamic_when: Fields are flat (no nesting beyond one level)

node_schema_fixed_vs_fixed_config.summary: Both can hide fields from the LLM, but they serve different purposes. Prefer node_schema+fixed for node fields; use fixed_config for purely operational/static values.

use_when: The field is a node config parameter (e.g. sandbox_mode, method, base_url)
You want the field explicitly present in the schema so its intent is clear
The field co-exists with LLM-visible fields in the same schema object
You want consistent schema documentation for the node
The value is purely operational and has no relevance to the LLM (e.g. api_key, base_url for a known endpoint)
You want a simple, flat override without declaring a full schema entry
Used together with $DYNAMIC placeholders for quick string-only cases

node_schema_fixed_vs_fixed_config.rule: If the field is a node behavioral parameter (affects how the node runs), use node_schema+fixed. If it is a static plumbing value (URL, key, method), fixed_config is fine. When in doubt, use node_schema+fixed — it is always correct.

http_request.summary: HTTP calls to external APIs. The most common node used as a tool. Fixed fields (URL, method, headers, auth) are hidden; the LLM supplies only the dynamic parameters.
special_behaviors: Extra non-reserved input keys with primitive values are automatically added as query params.
bearer_token input maps to the Authorization: Bearer header.
When secure: true in fixed_config, the response is hashed — the LLM never sees real tokens.
reserved_keys (never sent as query params): body, query_params, headers, base_url, endpoint, method, bearer_token, authorization, secure, __colmena_session_id, __node_id, __colmena_resume_answer

search_flights.description: Buscar vuelos disponibles entre dos aeropuertos en una fecha dada.

secure_token_then_use_pattern.description: Two-tool pattern: first tool obtains a token (marked secure: true so the LLM gets a placeholder), second tool uses that placeholder as the bearer. The engine resolves the placeholder to the real token at execution time.

get_token.name: get_token
get_token.description: Autenticar y obtener un token de acceso. Retorna un placeholder '<value_N>' que debes pasar a search_flights.

dynamic_placeholder_simple.when_to_use: All fields string + required + flat + 5 or fewer. Otherwise use node_schema.

create_comment.name: create_comment
create_comment.description: Crear un comentario en un post. Proporciona el body y el postId.

sql_query.summary: Execute SQL against a PostgreSQL database. Designed primarily as an LLM tool: the connection, permissions, and guardrails are fixed; the LLM supplies only the 'query' string. Supports a rich permission model and optional LLM-critic validation.
special_behaviors: When used as a tool, node_schema should fix 'connection_url' and 'permissions', exposing only 'query' to the LLM.
The 'auto_context' field injects live schema information into the LLM prompt automatically when set.
Permission presets: 'read_only' (SELECT only), 'read_write' (SELECT + INSERT + UPDATE + DELETE), 'full' (all including DDL).
tenant_user_id + auto_rls enable automatic row-level security without manual WHERE clauses.

read_only_query_tool.description: LLM can run any SELECT query. Connection and permissions are fixed.

query_db.name: query_db
query_db.description: Ejecutar una consulta SQL de solo lectura. Devuelve filas como JSON array.

query.description: Consulta SQL SELECT a ejecutar. Solo SELECT permitido.

read_write_with_rls.description: Read/write tool with automatic row-level security scoped to the current user.

manage_todos.name: manage_todos
manage_todos.description: Crear, leer, actualizar o eliminar tareas del usuario actual.

query.description: Consulta SQL (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE). Las filas se filtran automáticamente por user_id.

socketio_request.summary: Connect to a Socket.IO (WebSocket) server, emit an event with a JSON payload, and receive the response. The real-time counterpart to http_request — use it for event-driven APIs that use the Socket.IO protocol. As an LLM tool, fix url/namespace/event/cookies/timeout_ms in node_schema and expose only the dynamic payload fields the LLM should fill in.
socketio_request.see_also: docs/developer_guide/21_socketio_node.md — full guide with config reference, response patterns, pre_events, and troubleshooting.
special_behaviors: Stateless per execution: each tool call opens a fresh Socket.IO connection, emits, collects the response, and disconnects.
Two response patterns: ack mode (default — server replies via the Socket.IO acknowledgment callback) or wait-event mode (set 'wait_event' to listen for a separate named server event).
All string values support '${ENV_VAR}' resolution, including strings nested inside the payload (resolved recursively).
Errors are returned as an envelope, not exceptions: { success: false, event, error, exception? }. This lets downstream nodes branch on success.

pre_events: optional ordered list of events emitted on the SAME connection BEFORE the main event. Essential for servers that scope state per-socket (e.g., room subscriptions, sessions). On any pre-event failure the node aborts and never emits the main event — the envelope includes 'failed_pre_event' and the 'pre_responses' that did complete.
When in doubt about where to put non-LLM-visible fields, use node_schema with 'fixed' (the canonical pattern) — including the entire pre_events array, which the LLM should never see or modify.

load_canvas_state_with_wait_event.description: LLM tool that loads a canvas in one round-trip. The server replies via a separate broadcast event ('canvas_state_loaded'), so wait_event is set. All connection details are fixed; the LLM only triggers the call (no dynamic fields).

load_canvas.name: load_canvas
load_canvas.description: Load the current canvas state for the environment. Returns all existing nodes, edges, and groups.

mutation_with_pre_events.description: LLM tool that creates a node on a Socket.IO canvas. Because the server scopes mutation broadcasts to the room joined by the socket, the tool emits 'join_environment_room' as a pre_event on the SAME connection BEFORE 'create_node'. The pre_events array is fixed so the LLM cannot modify the auth/setup logic. The LLM only fills in the 'node' object inside payload.

create_canvas_node.name: create_canvas_node
create_canvas_node.description: Create a new node on the canvas. Returns the created node with its generated ID.

node.description: Node object: { type, category, position: {x,y}, data: { label, config? } }

ack_mode_simple.description: Minimal ack-mode tool — no wait_event, no pre_events. The server responds via the acknowledgment callback. Use this when the server's reply for the emitted event arrives via ack and no per-socket setup is needed.

ping_server.name: ping_server
ping_server.description: Send a ping to the realtime server and get back its current load metrics.

pre_events_with_wait_event_per_step.description: Two pre-events on the same socket, each with its OWN wait_event (one authenticates and waits for 'auth_ok', the other joins a room and waits for 'joined_room'), then the main event runs. Demonstrates per-step wait_event and per-step timeout_ms.

send_chat_message.name: send_chat_message
send_chat_message.description: Send a chat message to a private room.

text.description: Message text to send to the room.

tips: Default to node_schema + 'fixed' for url/namespace/event/cookies/timeout_ms — the LLM should never alter connection-level fields.
Use ack mode (omit wait_event) when the server replies via the Socket.IO acknowledgment callback. Use wait_event when the server emits a separate broadcast event as the response.

When the server scopes state per-socket (rooms, subscriptions, sessions), use pre_events to set up that state on the SAME connection before the main emit. Two separate socketio_request nodes will each open a fresh socket and lose the setup.

The pre_events array goes inside node_schema with 'fixed' so the LLM cannot disable or alter the auth/setup chain. Failure of any pre_event aborts the call cleanly with success=false and failed_pre_event.
Inputs override config fields with the same name — useful when chaining: a previous node can dynamically supply 'url' or 'payload' via edges while the rest stays fixed.
On error the node returns { success: false, event, error, ... } instead of throwing. Branch on success in downstream nodes if you want the LLM to react to failures.

tavily_client.summary: Toolkit node — exposes multiple sub-tools under a single alias. The LLM sees '<alias>__<subtool>' (e.g. 'web__search', 'web__fetch'). Use expose_sub_tools to control which sub-tools are available. The node_config block holds the Tavily API key and shared defaults; sub-tool parameters are passed by the LLM at call time.
special_behaviors: Toolkit nodes use expose_sub_tools instead of node_schema. The sub-tool schemas are defined inside the node itself.
Sub-tool names follow the pattern '<alias>__<subtool>' — e.g. if the map key is 'web', the LLM sees 'web__search' and 'web__fetch'.
search_defaults in node_config set fallback values for search calls; the LLM can override them per call.
Items in include_domains / exclude_domains must be strings (array of string).

search.description: Web search via Tavily. Returns ranked titles, URLs, and snippets.

include_content.description: Include full page content. 2-3x credit cost.

fetch.description: Read cleaned text from a URL. Use when you already know the URL.

all_sub_tools.description: Expose both search and fetch under the alias 'web'.

web_tool_id.name: web
web_tool_id.description: Web search and fetch via Tavily. Use web__search to find information, web__fetch to read a specific URL.

web.name: web
web.description: Buscar en la web información actualizada.

python_script.summary: Run a Python snippet as a tool. Two patterns: (A) Fixed code + LLM provides input variables. (B) LLM generates the code itself — use sandbox_mode: 'restricted' to validate it safely.
python_script.see_also: docs/developer_guide/26_python_node.md — full guide with architecture, threading model, troubleshooting.

reserved_keys.description: These three keys are consumed as node configuration and are NEVER injected as Python variables. Every other key in the schema becomes a global variable in the script.

special_behaviors: All inputs except the reserved keys ('code', 'sandbox_mode', 'sandbox_timeout_secs') are injected as Python global variables.
The script must assign its result to a variable named 'output'. Prefer a dict: output = {'count': 5, 'ids': [1,2,3]}. Returning null is allowed by simply not assigning 'output'.

When sandbox_mode is 'restricted': imports are validated against a whitelist (math, json, re, datetime, collections, itertools, functools, string, decimal, statistics); banned builtins (open, exec, eval, compile, __import__) are blocked; execution is capped at sandbox_timeout_secs (default 10s).
When sandbox_mode is 'none' (default): full Python access, no AST check, no timeout. Only use for trusted code, never for LLM-authored code.
On sandbox violation the node returns an error string ('SandboxViolation: ...') the LLM can read and retry with corrected code. SyntaxError is also surfaced.
Markdown code-block wrappers (```python ... ```) at the start/end of the code are stripped automatically — safe to feed raw LLM output into the 'code' field.
JSON objects/arrays passed via inputs become Python dicts/lists. Access with item['key'], not item.key.

fixed_code_llm_provides_variables.description: Pattern A — LLM provides a string; the script (fixed) transforms it. LLM never sees the code.

word_count.name: word_count
word_count.description: Contar las palabras en un texto.

llm_generates_code.description: Pattern B — LLM writes Python code AND passes the data to process as a tool argument. The LLM has already seen the data in a previous tool call (e.g. an HTTP response in its message history) and now passes it back along with the code. sandbox_mode is fixed so the LLM cannot weaken it. The script accesses 'rows' as a Python variable (from the LLM-supplied tool argument).

run_python.name: run_python
run_python.description: Ejecuta código Python para procesar una lista de datos que tú mismo provees. Pasa la lista en el argumento 'rows' y el código en 'code'. Asigna el resultado a 'output' como diccionario. Ejemplo: output = {'active': len([r for r in rows if r['stock'] > 0])}.

code.description: Código Python a ejecutar. Imports permitidos: math, json, re, datetime, collections, itertools, functools, string, decimal, statistics. NO uses os, sys, open, exec, eval. Asigna el resultado a 'output' como diccionario. Ejemplo: output = {'active': len([r for r in rows if r['stock'] > 0])}

rows.description: Lista de objetos a procesar. Pásale exactamente la lista que recibiste de un tool call previo (e.g. el HTTP response de search_products).

notes: In the current architecture, upstream node outputs do NOT auto-flow into a tool call. The LLM must include the data as a tool argument. This means the LLM has already seen the raw data in a previous turn — token cost is the trade-off for this minimal sandbox feature.
For token-efficient tool-to-tool piping (LLM never sees raw data), see the backlog: docs/superpowers/specs/python-tool-ideas-backlog.md.
Reserved keys (code, sandbox_mode, sandbox_timeout_secs) are the python_node config — everything else in the schema (e.g. 'rows') becomes a Python variable in the script.

Always pin sandbox_mode and sandbox_timeout_secs with 'fixed' so the LLM cannot weaken them. Always describe the allowed-imports list in the 'code' description so the LLM stays inside the whitelist on the first try.

fixed_logic_with_secret_constants.description: Variant of Pattern A — a fixed transform that uses constants the LLM should never see. Put the secret constants directly in 'code' as 'fixed', and only expose the user-facing argument.

score_lead.name: score_lead
score_lead.description: Compute a normalized lead score from a raw value 0-100.

tips: Prefer Pattern A when the transform is deterministic and known at design time. The LLM cannot break it.
Use Pattern B only when the transformation is open-ended (filtering, ad-hoc aggregation, JSON reshaping). Always fix sandbox_mode='restricted'.
For tools that need richer Python (numpy, pandas, requests) the python_script node is not the right tool — wrap your service in HTTP and use http_request as a tool.
Test sandboxed graphs locally with: cargo run --bin dag_engine -- run tests/graphs/agents/python_sandbox_tool_test.json

uuid_key_compatibility.description: Frontends often generate UUIDs as tool_configurations keys. Both UUID keys and semantic name keys work identically. The engine always uses the 'name' field inside the entry as the effective tool name — the map key is only a fallback.

example.comment: Both forms work. The LLM receives 'search_products' regardless of the map key.

system_prompt_auto_injection.description: When tool_configurations is non-empty and enabled_tools is active, the engine automatically appends a tool-use instruction block to the system_message. You do NOT need to include 'always use tools' instructions manually.
system_prompt_auto_injection.injected_block_template:
## Tool Use Instructions
You have access to the following tools:
- <tool_name_1>
- <tool_name_2>

Rules:
- ALWAYS use the available tools to answer questions that require real or live data. Never answer from your own knowledge when a tool can provide the data.
- Call the most relevant tool before responding. Do not skip tool calls.
- If a tool call fails, report the error clearly instead of guessing an answer.
- Only respond without a tool call when the user's request is purely conversational and no tool is needed.
system_prompt_auto_injection.implication: Your system_message only needs to describe the agent's role and behavior — the tool instructions are managed by the engine.

deprecated_fields.note: These fields still work for backward compatibility but must not be used in new configurations. Use node_schema instead.

fields.exposed_inputs: Array of input names to expose to the LLM.
fields.parameters: Manual JSON Schema override for tool parameters.
fields.mergeable_fields: Fields where fixed + dynamic values are merged rather than overridden.
fields.field_mapping: Maps each LLM parameter to its destination container field.
